title: Bank Treasury Architecture: Integrated Treasury Operations, Dealing Room Protocols, Front-Mid-Back Office Segregation & CRR / SLR Compliance
description: Master institutional bank treasury management and statutory reserve operations. Analyze the modern integrated treasury model across domestic money market, foreign exchange (Forex), and fixed-income securities desks, enforce strict Chinese Walls and three-way organizational segregation among Front, Mid, and Back offices, compute Net Demand and Time Liabilities (NDTL) under central bank guidelines, engineer daily Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) fortnightly maintenance schedules to eliminate penal interest and minimize negative carry, structure the Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) portfolio across Held to Maturity (HTM), Available for Sale (AFS), and Held for Trading (HFT) accounting categories, and implement market risk limits including Net Open Position Limits (NOPL), PV01, and stop-loss governance.
goal: Equip bank treasury directors, ALM desk heads, and market risk officers to manage multi-billion-dollar bank liquidity, ensure flawless CRR/SLR compliance, and deploy dealing room risk limit architectures.
recap: In Block 7, we conquered wholesale corporate lending, syndications, and project finance. In Block 8, we step into the nerve center of commercial banking: the Bank Treasury, where billions of dollars in liquidity, foreign exchange, sovereign debt, and statutory reserves are traded and hedged every second.

parts.title: The Integrated Treasury Architecture: Desks, Liquidity Mandates & Front-Mid-Back Office Segregation
say: In historical commercial banking, treasury was regarded as a passive, non-revenue administrative cost center whose sole obligation was to hold idle cash reserves to comply with statutory central bank directives. Over the past three decades of financial liberalization, interest rate deregulation, and cross-border capital flows, bank treasury has undergone a radical metamorphosis into the Integrated Bank Treasury. Today, the treasury department represents the supreme financial engine, strategic nerve center, and primary profitability driver of a commercial bank. The integrated treasury seamlessly unifies domestic money market operations, sovereign and corporate debt trading, foreign exchange dealing, and interest rate derivatives into a consolidated dealing room platform, optimizing enterprise-wide balance sheet liquidity while extracting trading alpha across international financial markets.

The Three Operational Pillars of Integrated Treasury: An institutional treasury orchestrates three distinct yet interconnected dealing desks: (1) The Domestic Money Market Desk: Responsible for enterprise liquidity management, intraday central bank clearing, Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) maintenance, call/notice money borrowing, Commercial Paper (CP), Certificates of Deposit (CD), and Tri-Party Repo (TREPS) transactions; (2) The Forex Dealing Desk: Executing cross-currency spot, forward, swap, and options transactions, managing merchant export-import flows, handling currency conversions, and maintaining sovereign currency Nostro account balances; and (3) The Fixed Income & Derivatives Desk: Managing the bank's massive statutory and non-statutory securities investment portfolios, trading Central and State Government Securities (G-Secs and SDLs), underwriting corporate debt placements, and executing interest rate swaps (IRS) and forward rate agreements (FRAs) to hedge balance sheet interest rate mismatches.

The Principle of Organizational Segregation (Chinese Walls): Because treasury dealing rooms handle hundreds of millions of dollars in uncollateralized transactions daily and possess access to confidential client flow information, regulatory authorities and global Basel standards mandate an absolute, non-negotiable operational separation known as the 'Three-Tier Functional Architecture' or 'Chinese Wall'. The treasury is strictly compartmentalized into three independent divisions: Front Office, Mid Office, and Back Office, reporting to completely separate executive hierarchies.

Front Office (Deal Execution & Trading Floor): The Front Office comprises licensed traders, dealers, and portfolio managers seated on the dealing floor, operating dealing terminals (such as Bloomberg, Refinitiv, and central bank order matching platforms like NDS-OM). Their mandate is deal origination, customer order execution, price discovery, and active market-making within pre-approved trading limits. Traders have zero authority to confirm trades with counterparties, modify accounting ledgers, or settle fund transfers. All phone lines and trading chat terminals are recorded on tamper-evident digital logging servers.

Mid Office / Market Risk Management (Independent Oversight & Limit Control): The Mid Office serves as the independent risk controller and compliance watchdog of the dealing room, reporting directly to the Chief Risk Officer (CRO) and the Asset-Liability Committee (ALCO). The Mid Office operates completely separated from trading profit incentives. Its mandate includes: real-time monitoring of dealer limits, Net Open Position Limits (NOPL), daylight and overnight counterparty limits, Value at Risk (VaR) calculations, stop-loss trigger enforcement, marked-to-market (MTM) daily portfolio revaluations, and exception reporting to senior management.

Back Office / Treasury Settlements & Accounting (Verification & Movement of Funds): The Back Office is the operational and settlement engine, reporting independently to the Chief Financial Officer (CFO). Once a trader executes a deal in the Front Office, the deal ticket electronically routes to the Back Office. The Back Office independently verifies deal terms with the counterparty through authenticated SWIFT messages (such as MT300 for Forex or MT540/MT541 for securities), executes payments via central bank RTGS or clearing corporations (such as CCIL), manages collateral margins, handles daily Nostro and Vostro account reconciliations, and books accounting journal entries in the core banking ledger.

By establishing unbreachable Chinese Walls among the Front, Mid, and Back offices, commercial banks unleash dynamic trading revenue generation while establishing an impenetrable operational defense against rogue trading, insider manipulation, and settlement failure.
parts.example: A trader executes a $50M spot USD/INR trade on the Refinitiv terminal in the Front Office. The Mid Office instantly registers the $50M utilization against the bank's Net Open Position Limit. The Back Office receives the electronic ticket, cross-checks the SWIFT MT300 confirmation with the counterparty bank, and releases funds via RTGS, with no trader involvement in settlement.
parts.code:
def evaluate_treasury_segregation_and_deal_flow(
    deal_id: str = "FX-2026-8941",
    instrument_type: str = "SPOT_USD_INR",
    notional_amount_usd: float = 50000000.0,
    dealer_limit_usd: float = 75000000.0,
    current_nopl_exposure_usd: float = 40000000.0,
    nopl_cap_usd: float = 100000000.0,
    front_office_executed: bool = True,
    mid_office_risk_approved: bool = True,
    back_office_swift_matched: bool = True
) -> dict:
    # Integrated Bank Treasury 3-Tier Chinese Wall Validation Engine
    
    # 1. Front Office Dealer Limit Check
    dealer_limit_cleared = notional_amount_usd <= dealer_limit_usd
    
    # 2. Mid Office Market Risk & NOPL Check
    pro_forma_nopl = current_nopl_exposure_usd + notional_amount_usd
    nopl_limit_cleared = pro_forma_nopl <= nopl_cap_usd
    mid_office_gate = mid_office_risk_approved and nopl_limit_cleared
    
    # 3. Back Office Independent Settlement Gate
    back_office_gate = back_office_swift_matched and not (front_office_executed and False) # Strictly separate personnel
    
    # Overall Institutional Deal Settlement Clearance
    deal_cleared = dealer_limit_cleared and mid_office_gate and back_office_gate
    
    return {
        'deal_id': deal_id,
        'instrument': instrument_type,
        'notional_usd': notional_amount_usd,
        'dealer_limit_cleared': dealer_limit_cleared,
        'pro_forma_nopl_usd': pro_forma_nopl,
        'nopl_headroom_remaining': max(0.0, nopl_cap_usd - pro_forma_nopl),
        'mid_office_risk_gate': mid_office_gate,
        'back_office_settlement_gate': back_office_gate,
        'three_tier_chinese_wall_verified': True,
        'deal_settlement_status': 'AUTHORIZED_FOR_RTGS_SETTLEMENT' if deal_cleared else 'SETTLEMENT_BLOCKED_BY_RISK_CONTROL'
    }

treasury_deal = evaluate_treasury_segregation_and_deal_flow()
print("=== Integrated Bank Treasury - 3-Tier Functional Architecture Docket ===")
print(f"Treasury Deal Identification:   {treasury_deal['deal_id']} ({treasury_deal['instrument']})")
print(f"Notional Value Traded:          ${treasury_deal['notional_usd']:,.2f}")
print(f"Front Office Dealer Authority:  {treasury_deal['dealer_limit_cleared']} (Within $75M Limit)")
print(f"Pro-Forma NOPL Exposure:        ${treasury_deal['pro_forma_nopl_usd']:,.2f} (Cap: $100M)")
print(f"Remaining NOPL Headroom:        ${treasury_deal['nopl_headroom_remaining']:,.2f}")
print(f"Mid Office Risk Clearance:      {treasury_deal['mid_office_risk_gate']}")
print(f"Back Office SWIFT Confirmation: {treasury_deal['back_office_settlement_gate']}")
print(f"Chinese Wall Isolation Audit:   {treasury_deal['three_tier_chinese_wall_verified']}")
print(f"Final Deal Execution Verdict:   {treasury_deal['deal_settlement_status']}")

check.question: What is the primary regulatory rationale for strictly enforcing Chinese Walls among Front, Mid, and Back offices in a bank treasury?
options: To prevent rogue trading and balance sheet fraud by ensuring dealers who execute transactions have zero authority to confirm trades, revalue portfolios, or disburse settlement funds.
To ensure that traders can settle their own trades faster without paperwork.
To eliminate the need for computer systems on the trading floor.
To allow the bank to avoid paying federal taxes on trading profits.
check.why: Strict three-way operational segregation prevents conflict of interest and rogue trading by ensuring independent trade verification, risk limit monitoring, and settlement.

parts.title: Statutory Reserve Physics: CRR Formulation, Maintenance Floors & Penal Structures
say: Commercial banks possess the unique, sovereign-delegated license to create money through fractional reserve lending. However, this power creates an inherent systemic fragility: banks borrow on instantaneous demand while extending long-term illiquid loans. To ensure systemic liquidity, anchor monetary policy transmission, and insulate depositor funds, central banks enforce mandatory statutory reserve requirements. The foremost statutory lever is the Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR)—a non-negotiable cash balance that commercial banks must maintain in current accounts with the Central Bank, bearing zero interest.

Formulation of Net Demand and Time Liabilities (NDTL): The statutory baseline against which all reserve requirements are calculated is the bank's Net Demand and Time Liabilities (NDTL). Under statutory banking regulations (such as Section 42 of the RBI Act), NDTL is derived through an exhaustive balance sheet formula: NDTL = Demand Liabilities + Time Liabilities + Other Demand & Time Liabilities - Deductions. Demand Liabilities include Current Account deposits, Savings Account deposits (the demand component of CASA), overdue fixed deposits, unpaid demand drafts, and telegraphic transfers. Time Liabilities comprise term fixed deposits, cumulative deposits, and recurring deposits. Other Demand and Time Liabilities (ODTL) incorporate accrued interest on deposits, staff security deposits, and credit balances in suspense accounts.

Permissible Deductions & Inter-Bank Exclusions: To prevent double-counting across the banking sector, statutory guidelines permit specific deductions: (1) Balances held in current accounts with other domestic commercial banks; (2) Inter-bank term deposits placed with other banks up to the maturity of inter-bank borrowings; and (3) Inward remittance transit adjustments. The resulting figure establishes the bank's net external depositor liability base (NDTL).

The Mechanics of Fortnightly Maintenance: Commercial banks maintain CRR on a 14-day cycle known as the 'Reporting Fortnight', spanning from a Saturday to the second following Friday (the 'Reporting Friday'). If a bank's NDTL is audited at $40,000,000,000 and the statutory CRR rate is set at 4.50%, the bank's mandatory average daily CRR balance is exactly $1,800,000,000. Over the 14-day fortnight, the bank must accumulate an aggregate product of $25,200,000,000 ($1.8B * 14 days).

The Daily Minimum Maintenance Floor (Negative Carry Optimization): Because bank deposit balances fluctuate daily due to corporate tax outflows, loan disbursements, and clearing swings, central banks permit daily flexibility. Rather than maintaining the exact $1.8B every single day, the bank is permitted to maintain a fluctuating balance, subject to an immutable Daily Minimum Floor—typically set at ninety percent (90%) of the required daily average ($1,620,000,000). Treasury cash managers exploit this flexibility through negative carry optimization: because CRR balances earn zero percent interest while overnight money market lending yields 6.50%, treasurers intentionally maintain near the 90% floor during the early days of the fortnight, lending excess cash into call money or TREPS markets to earn overnight interest, before topping up balances on the final days to satisfy the 14-day cumulative target.

Standing Deposit Facility (SDF) vs Non-Remunerated Reserves: In contemporary liquidity management, central banks operate standing facilities alongside statutory CRR. Under modern liquidity frameworks, commercial banks with overnight surplus funds beyond statutory CRR requirements can park uncollateralized liquidity at the Standing Deposit Facility (SDF) at a non-zero interest rate (typically pegged at Policy Repo Rate minus 25 bps). Treasury desks must rigorously distinguish between the unremunerated statutory CRR account—which yields zero return and penalizes shortfalls—and interest-bearing overnight central bank absorption rails like the SDF, ensuring that every dollar of liquidity above the statutory maintenance schedule is deployed into earning assets.

Severe Penal Interest Structures for Default: Failure to maintain statutory CRR carries draconian regulatory consequences. Under central bank statutory codes, if a bank defaults on its daily 90% floor or fortnightly cumulative target, it is slapped with statutory penal interest: Bank Rate + 300 basis points (e.g. 6.75% + 3.00% = 9.75%) on the shortfall for the first day, escalating to Bank Rate + 500 basis points (11.75%) for subsequent days of default. Furthermore, executive directors are liable for regulatory censure, and the central bank possesses statutory powers to prohibit the bank from accepting fresh deposits or declaring shareholder dividends.

By commanding the mathematics of NDTL computation, fortnightly product accumulation, and daily floor dynamics, bank treasury directors optimize cash yields while maintaining an ironclad perimeter against statutory reserve defaults.
parts.example: A bank with $40B NDTL has a 4.5% CRR requirement ($1.8B daily average, $25.2B 14-day product). The treasurer maintains $1.62B (the 90% floor) on Day 1, lending the $180M surplus into overnight TREPS at 6.50% to earn $32,500 in overnight profit, and tops up the balance later in the fortnight.
parts.code:
def calculate_crr_fortnightly_schedule(
    total_demand_liabilities: float = 18000000000.0,
    total_time_liabilities: float = 24000000000.0,
    other_demand_time_liab: float = 1000000000.0,
    inter_bank_assets_deduction: float = 3000000000.0,
    crr_statutory_rate: float = 0.045,
    daily_minimum_floor_pct: float = 0.90,
    overnight_money_market_rate: float = 0.065,
    bank_rate: float = 0.0675
) -> dict:
    # Statutory Reserve Engine: NDTL & CRR Fortnightly Formulation
    gross_liabilities = total_demand_liabilities + total_time_liabilities + other_demand_time_liab
    ndtl = gross_liabilities - inter_bank_assets_deduction
    
    daily_crr_requirement = ndtl * crr_statutory_rate
    fortnightly_product_requirement = daily_crr_requirement * 14
    daily_min_floor_balance = daily_crr_requirement * daily_minimum_floor_pct
    
    # Negative Carry Yield Optimization (Lending surplus down to 90% floor on Day 1)
    optimizable_day1_surplus = daily_crr_requirement - daily_min_floor_balance
    day1_overnight_interest_earned = optimizable_day1_surplus * (overnight_money_market_rate / 365.0)
    
    # Penal Rates for Default Reference
    penal_rate_day1 = bank_rate + 0.03
    penal_rate_subsequent = bank_rate + 0.05
    
    return {
        'audited_ndtl': ndtl,
        'crr_rate_pct': crr_statutory_rate * 100,
        'daily_average_crr_required': daily_crr_requirement,
        'fortnightly_product_target': fortnightly_product_requirement,
        'daily_90pct_minimum_floor': daily_min_floor_balance,
        'optimizable_day1_surplus': optimizable_day1_surplus,
        'day1_interest_earned_at_floor': day1_overnight_interest_earned,
        'penal_rate_day1_pct': penal_rate_day1 * 100,
        'penal_rate_subsequent_pct': penal_rate_subsequent * 100
    }

crr_sched = calculate_crr_fortnightly_schedule()
print("=== Statutory Reserve Formulation: NDTL & CRR Schedule Docket ===")
print(f"Audited Bank NDTL Base:        ${crr_sched['audited_ndtl']:,.2f}")
print(f"Statutory CRR Rate:            {crr_sched['crr_rate_pct']:.2f}%")
print(f"Daily Average CRR Requirement: ${crr_sched['daily_average_crr_required']:,.2f}")
print(f"14-Day Cumulative Product:     ${crr_sched['fortnightly_product_target']:,.2f}")
print(f"Daily 90% Minimum Floor:       ${crr_sched['daily_90pct_minimum_floor']:,.2f}")
print(f"Lendable Surplus to 90% Floor: ${crr_sched['optimizable_day1_surplus']:,.2f}")
print(f"Day 1 Overnight Interest Gain: ${crr_sched['day1_interest_earned_at_floor']:,.2f}")
print(f"Statutory Penal Rate (Day 1):  {crr_sched['penal_rate_day1_pct']:.2f}% (Bank Rate + 300 bps)")
print(f"Statutory Penal Rate (Subseq): {crr_sched['penal_rate_subsequent_pct']:.2f}% (Bank Rate + 500 bps)")

parts.title: Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) & Portfolio Accounting: HTM, AFS & HFT Categories
say: While the Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) mandates zero-yielding cash balances at the central bank, the Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) constitutes the second structural pillar of bank reserve governance. Governed under Section 24 of the Banking Regulation Act, SLR mandates that every commercial bank maintain an unencumbered percentage of its Net Demand and Time Liabilities (NDTL)—currently set at 18.00%—in specified High-Quality Liquid Assets (HQLA). Unlike CRR, SLR assets are interest-earning investments held directly on the bank's own balance sheet, forming the bedrock of national sovereign debt absorption and secondary liquidity defense.

Eligible Statutory Liquidity Assets: Under statutory prudential guidelines, only three asset categories qualify for SLR compliance: (1) Cash in Hand: Physical currency notes and coins stored in bank vaults and automated teller machine (ATM) cassettes; (2) Sovereign Gold Reserves: Gold bullion and coins valued at current market rates not exceeding current market prices; and (3) Unencumbered Approved Government Securities: Primarily Central Government Dated Securities (G-Secs), Treasury Bills (91-day, 182-day, and 364-day T-Bills), and State Development Loans (SDLs). Crucially, securities pledged to borrow funds in repo markets or posted as collateral with clearing corporations are 'encumbered' and strictly disqualified from SLR counting.

The Three-Tier Investment Accounting Architecture (HTM, AFS & HFT): To balance statutory stability against market price volatility, bank treasuries segregate their multi-billion-dollar securities portfolios into three regulatory accounting buckets: Held to Maturity (HTM), Available for Sale (AFS), and Held for Trading (HFT).

Held to Maturity (HTM): Securities acquired with the explicit institutional intention of being held until final redemption are booked in HTM. Up to a statutory cap (historically 25% of total investments, or specific regulatory carve-outs up to 19.5% of NDTL for statutory securities), banks can shield HTM bonds from mark-to-market (MTM) accounting volatility. HTM securities are NOT marked to market on balance sheet dates; instead, they are carried at amortized acquisition cost. Any premium paid over face value is amortized over the remaining maturity, insulating bank equity and Profit & Loss (P&L) statements from rising interest rate bond price collapses.

Available for Sale (AFS) & Held for Trading (HFT): Securities acquired for liquidity management or active market trading fall into AFS and HFT. HFT securities are acquired with the intention of profiting from short-term price movements and must be liquidated within 90 days. Both AFS and HFT portfolios MUST be marked to market (revalued) at regular intervals—daily for HFT and at least quarterly for AFS—based on fair market yield curves published by the Fixed Income Money Market and Derivatives Association (FIMMDA) or Financial Benchmarks India Pvt Ltd (FBIL).

Basel III LCR Alignment & Carve-Out Facilities (MSF & FALLCR): Under the Basel III regulatory framework, banks must maintain a Liquidity Coverage Ratio (LCR) ensuring sufficient unencumbered High-Quality Liquid Assets (HQLA) to survive a 30-day catastrophic liquidity stress. Because holding both 18% SLR and a separate LCR portfolio would immobilize prohibitive volumes of bank capital, central banks allow specific SLR carve-outs to qualify as Level 1 HQLA. Specifically, banks are permitted to count government securities held under the Marginal Standing Facility (MSF—typically 2% of NDTL) and the Facility to Avail Liquidity for Liquidity Coverage Ratio (FALLCR—typically 15% to 16% of NDTL) directly toward their Basel III HQLA requirement, harmonizing domestic statutory liquidity mandates with global liquidity standards.

Asymmetric MTM Accounting & Investment Fluctuation Reserve (IFR): Under conservative prudential accounting rules, MTM revaluation follows asymmetric conservatism: Net depreciation across each classification category must be fully recognized and charged as an expense in the P&L statement, whereas net appreciation CANNOT be credited to P&L or taken to equity reserves, but must be ignored. To protect the bank against future interest rate shocks, banks are mandated to build an Investment Fluctuation Reserve (IFR) of at least two percent (2.0%) of their combined AFS and HFT portfolios out of retained profits, qualifying as Tier-2 regulatory capital.

By commanding SLR asset eligibility, HTM amortized accounting insulation, and AFS/HFT mark-to-market mechanics, treasury officers optimize portfolio yields while safeguarding bank solvency against interest rate volatility.
parts.example: A bank with $40B NDTL maintains an 18% SLR ($7.2B). It allocates $5.0B in G-Secs to HTM (carried at amortized cost, shielding P&L from rate hikes) and $2.2B in T-Bills to AFS (marked to market daily). If 10-year G-Sec yields jump 50 bps, the $5.0B HTM portfolio incurs zero P&L write-down.
parts.code:
def evaluate_slr_portfolio_allocation_and_mtm(
    ndtl_base: float = 40000000000.0,
    slr_mandate_pct: float = 0.18,
    actual_gsec_portfolio_cost: float = 8000000000.0,
    htm_allocation_pct: float = 0.65,
    afs_allocation_pct: float = 0.35,
    yield_increase_bps: float = 50.0,
    afs_modified_duration: float = 3.5
) -> dict:
    # Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) & MTM Valuation Engine
    mandatory_slr_amount = ndtl_base * slr_mandate_pct
    slr_surplus_cushion = actual_gsec_portfolio_cost - mandatory_slr_amount
    
    # Portfolio Segregation
    htm_book_value = actual_gsec_portfolio_cost * htm_allocation_pct
    afs_book_value = actual_gsec_portfolio_cost * afs_allocation_pct
    
    # Mark-to-Market (MTM) Sensitivity on AFS Portfolio
    # Bond Price Change % ~= -Modified Duration * Delta Yield
    delta_yield = yield_increase_bps / 10000.0
    afs_price_change_pct = -afs_modified_duration * delta_yield
    afs_mtm_loss = afs_book_value * abs(afs_price_change_pct)
    
    # HTM is insulated from MTM (0 write-down)
    htm_mtm_loss = 0.0
    total_pnl_hit = afs_mtm_loss
    
    # Mandatory Investment Fluctuation Reserve (IFR: 2% of AFS/HFT)
    mandatory_ifr_required = afs_book_value * 0.02
    
    return {
        'ndtl_base': ndtl_base,
        'mandatory_slr_required': mandatory_slr_amount,
        'total_gsec_held': actual_gsec_portfolio_cost,
        'slr_surplus_buffer': slr_surplus_cushion,
        'htm_insulated_portfolio': htm_book_value,
        'afs_market_sensitive_portfolio': afs_book_value,
        'yield_shock_bps': yield_increase_bps,
        'afs_price_decline_pct': round(afs_price_change_pct * 100, 3),
        'afs_pnl_hit': round(afs_mtm_loss, 2),
        'htm_pnl_hit': htm_mtm_loss,
        'total_pnl_devaluation': round(total_pnl_hit, 2),
        'mandatory_ifr_reserve': round(mandatory_ifr_required, 2)
    }

slr_eval = evaluate_slr_portfolio_allocation_and_mtm()
print("=== Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) & Portfolio Accounting Docket ===")
print(f"Bank NDTL Assessment Base:      ${slr_eval['ndtl_base']:,.2f}")
print(f"Mandatory SLR Requirement (18%): ${slr_eval['mandatory_slr_required']:,.2f}")
print(f"Total G-Sec Portfolio Held:     ${slr_eval['total_gsec_held']:,.2f}")
print(f"SLR Surplus Liquidity Buffer:   ${slr_eval['slr_surplus_buffer']:,.2f} (Available for repo)")
print(f" - Held to Maturity (HTM - 65%):${slr_eval['htm_insulated_portfolio']:,.2f} (Amortized Cost)")
print(f" - Available for Sale (AFS - 35%):${slr_eval['afs_market_sensitive_portfolio']:,.2f} (MTM Revalued)")
print(f"Adverse Yield Shock Modeled:    +{slr_eval['yield_shock_bps']} bps")
print(f"AFS Portfolio Price Decline:    {slr_eval['afs_price_decline_pct']}%")
print(f"AFS Mark-to-Market P&L Hit:     ${slr_eval['afs_pnl_hit']:,.2f}")
print(f"HTM Mark-to-Market P&L Hit:     ${slr_eval['htm_pnl_hit']:,.2f} (Fully Insulated!)")
print(f"Total Balance Sheet P&L Charge: ${slr_eval['total_pnl_devaluation']:,.2f}")
print(f"Mandatory 2% IFR Reserve:       ${slr_eval['mandatory_ifr_reserve']:,.2f}")

parts.title: Dealing Room Risk Limits: Daylight, Overnight, Stop-Loss & PV01 Governance
say: A bank treasury operates directly at the interface of volatile global financial markets: currency exchange rates fluctuate tick-by-tick, sovereign bond yields gyrate on central bank announcements, and interbank liquidity tightens without warning. In the absence of rigid, automated, and mathematically enforced risk limits, a single undisciplined trader can jeopardize the capital of the entire institution. To govern trading exposures, the Mid Office enforces a comprehensive dealing room market risk architecture consisting of position limits, sensitivity metrics, and loss mitigation protocols.

Position Limits: Daylight Limits & Net Open Position Limits (NOPL): The most fundamental market risk control is the Net Open Position Limit (NOPL), governing the bank's aggregate net unhedged foreign exchange exposure across all foreign currencies. The Mid Office enforces two distinct position boundaries: (1) Daylight Limit: The maximum net open position dealers are permitted to hold during active trading hours, allowing intra-day liquidity provision and client order matching; and (2) Overnight Limit (NOPL): A much more restrictive limit enforced at the close of the trading day. Because market news, geopolitical conflicts, and overnight interest rate changes can occur while domestic markets are closed, the overnight limit is tightly capped (typically capped by the central bank at a percentage of Tier-1 capital, e.g. $100M). Any excess daylight exposure must be squared off or hedged before the closing bell.

Gap Limits: Individual Gap Limits (IGL) & Aggregate Gap Limits (AGL): Forex positions carry forward delivery date mismatches. For example, a trader may be long USD 100M for 1-month maturity and short USD 100M for 3-month maturity. Although the net position is zero, the bank is exposed to interest rate parity shifts between the two maturities. The Mid Office establishes Individual Gap Limits (IGL) capping the net mismatch in any individual forward month, and an Aggregate Gap Limit (AGL) capping total mismatches across all forward buckets.

Counterparty Settlement Risk & Herstatt Risk (CLS Netting): When executing multi-million-dollar cross-border foreign exchange transactions across different time zones, the bank is exposed to catastrophic Settlement Risk (historically immortalized as 'Herstatt Risk', where a bank pays out domestic currency in one time zone but the foreign counterparty collapses before delivering foreign currency in its own time zone). To mitigate this existential threat, the Mid Office enforces Pre-Settlement Risk (PSR) limits and Settlement Risk (SR) limits for every approved counterparty. Furthermore, treasury operations channel cross-border currency settlements through Continuous Linked Settlement (CLS) Bank rails, executing transactions on a simultaneous Payment-versus-Payment (PvP) basis that eliminates cross-currency principal settlement risk.

Price Value of a Basis Point (PV01 / DV01): In fixed-income securities trading, portfolio managers do not measure risk in gross face value; they measure it in Price Value of a Basis Point (PV01, also termed Dollar Value of a 01, DV01). PV01 quantifies the exact absolute dollar change in portfolio market value resulting from a one-basis-point (0.01% or 0.0001) shift in interest rate yields: PV01 = (Portfolio Value at Yield - 1 bp) - (Portfolio Value at Yield + 1 bp) / 2. A treasury bond portfolio with a PV01 of $250,000 will gain $2,500,000 if bond yields fall by 10 bps, but will lose an identical $2,500,000 if yields jump by 10 bps. The Mid Office sets non-negotiable PV01 caps across each trading desk to limit interest rate vulnerability.

Value at Risk (VaR) & Stop-Loss Architecture: To capture multi-asset statistical risk, banks deploy Value at Risk (VaR). A 1-day 99% VaR of $5,000,000 indicates that under normal market conditions, the desk's daily trading loss will not exceed $5,000,000 in ninety-nine out of one hundred trading days. If market volatility spikes, the final operational safety net is the Stop-Loss Architecture: enforced at three cascading levels: (1) Dealer-Level Daily Stop-Loss (e.g. $100,000); (2) Desk-Level Monthly Stop-Loss (e.g. $1,000,000); and (3) Treasury-Wide Cumulative Stop-Loss (e.g. $5,000,000). When a stop-loss threshold is breached, the Mid Office instantly revokes trading terminal access, freezes open orders, and initiates mandatory trade unwinds.
By commanding the mathematics of NOPL, gap limits, PV01 sensitivities, VaR modeling, and stop-loss execution, treasury risk managers maintain airtight control over multi-billion-dollar trading books.
parts.example: A fixed income desk holds $1B in 10-year G-Secs with a PV01 of $650,000. If central bank commentary pushes benchmark yields up by 8 bps, the desk incurs an immediate marked-to-market loss of $5.2M ($650K * 8 bps). The desk stop-loss of $6.0M holds, avoiding a mandatory portfolio freeze.
parts.code:
def evaluate_treasury_market_risk_limits(
    portfolio_market_value: float = 1000000000.0,
    portfolio_modified_duration: float = 6.5,
    daily_var_99_limit_usd: float = 8000000.0,
    desk_stop_loss_limit_usd: float = 6000000.0,
    intraday_yield_spike_bps: float = 8.0,
    current_nopl_usd: float = 85000000.0,
    overnight_nopl_cap_usd: float = 100000000.0
) -> dict:
    # Treasury Market Risk & PV01 Limit Engine
    
    # 1. PV01 Calculation: Value change per 1 bp (0.0001) shift
    # PV01 ~= Portfolio Value * Modified Duration * 0.0001
    pv01_usd = portfolio_market_value * portfolio_modified_duration * 0.0001
    
    # 2. Daily MTM Impact from Yield Spike
    mtm_impact_usd = pv01_usd * intraday_yield_spike_bps
    
    # 3. Stop-Loss & VaR Limit Checks
    is_stop_loss_breached = mtm_impact_usd >= desk_stop_loss_limit_usd
    is_var_breached = mtm_impact_usd >= daily_var_99_limit_usd
    
    # 4. Overnight NOPL Check
    is_nopl_compliant = current_nopl_usd <= overnight_nopl_cap_usd
    
    all_risk_limits_healthy = (not is_stop_loss_breached) and (not is_var_breached) and is_nopl_compliant
    
    return {
        'portfolio_value': portfolio_market_value,
        'modified_duration': portfolio_modified_duration,
        'pv01_sensitivity_usd': round(pv01_usd, 2),
        'yield_shift_bps': intraday_yield_spike_bps,
        'intraday_mtm_loss_usd': round(mtm_impact_usd, 2),
        'stop_loss_limit': desk_stop_loss_limit_usd,
        'is_stop_loss_breached': is_stop_loss_breached,
        'is_var_breached': is_var_breached,
        'current_nopl_usd': current_nopl_usd,
        'is_nopl_compliant': is_nopl_compliant,
        'trading_desk_status': 'NORMAL_OPERATIONS' if all_risk_limits_healthy else 'MANDATORY_UNWIND_TRIGGERED'
    }

risk_eval = evaluate_treasury_market_risk_limits()
print("=== Bank Treasury Dealing Room Market Risk Limits Docket ===")
print(f"Fixed Income Trading Book Value: ${risk_eval['portfolio_value']:,.2f}")
print(f"Portfolio Modified Duration:    {risk_eval['modified_duration']} years")
print(f"Calculated PV01 Sensitivity:    ${risk_eval['pv01_sensitivity_usd']:,.2f} per basis point")
print(f"Intraday Yield Shift Observed:  +{risk_eval['yield_shift_bps']} bps")
print(f"Intraday MTM Portfolio Impact:  -${risk_eval['intraday_mtm_loss_usd']:,.2f}")
print(f"Desk Stop-Loss Limit:           ${risk_eval['stop_loss_limit']:,.2f}")
print(f"Stop-Loss Trigger Breached:     {risk_eval['is_stop_loss_breached']}")
print(f"Daily 99% VaR Breached:         {risk_eval['is_var_breached']}")
print(f"Overnight NOPL Status:          ${risk_eval['current_nopl_usd']:,.2f} (Compliant: {risk_eval['is_nopl_compliant']})")
print(f"Trading Desk Risk Authorization:{risk_eval['trading_desk_status']}")

parts.title: Comprehensive Enterprise Bank Treasury & CRR/SLR Compliance Simulator
say: In this capstone operational phase of Day 36, we synthesize the entire bank treasury architecture, reserve maintenance physics, and risk limit frameworks into an institutional treasury command simulator. You assume the executive authority of Group Treasurer at Titan National Bank, commanding the liquidity, investment, and market risk operations of a $50,000,000,000 commercial banking balance sheet during an intense macroeconomic clearing cycle.

Auditing Balance Sheet Liabilities & Statutory Baselines: Titan National Bank's balance sheet reflects gross Demand Liabilities of $20,000,000,000 (Current Accounts, Savings Accounts, overdue deposits), gross Time Liabilities of $28,000,000,000 (fixed term deposits), and Other Demand and Time Liabilities of $2,000,000,000. Permissible inter-bank deductions equal $5,000,000,000. The treasury engine computes net external depositor liabilities (NDTL) at an audited $45,000,000,000.

Deploying Statutory Reserve Allocations: Against the $45B NDTL base, statutory mandates require: (1) Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR @ 4.50%): Daily average required balance of $2,025,000,000 maintained in unremunerated cash accounts with the central bank, with an absolute daily minimum 90% floor of $1,822,500,000; and (2) Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR @ 18.00%): Mandatory unencumbered HQLA portfolio of $8,100,000,000. Titan Treasury maintains an actual G-Sec and T-Bill portfolio of $9,500,000,000, establishing a massive $1,400,000,000 surplus SLR liquidity buffer.

Structuring Investment Accounting Buckets: To insulate capital from yield volatility while maintaining tactical trading flexibility, the Group Treasurer segments the $9.5B securities portfolio: (1) Held to Maturity (HTM): $6,175,000,000 (65%), carried at amortized cost; (2) Available for Sale (AFS): $2,850,000,000 (30%), marked to market quarterly with a PV01 of $1,140,000; and (3) Held for Trading (HFT): $475,000,000 (5%), marked to market daily with an intraday PV01 of $95,000.

Funds Transfer Pricing (FTP) & Asset-Liability Committee (ALCO) Alignment: As Group Treasurer, you maintain strategic cohesion across the commercial bank through the Funds Transfer Pricing (FTP) mechanism. Treasury acts as the internal central bank for the institution: buying deposits from retail branches and selling liquidity to commercial corporate lending units. By setting transparent, maturity-matched FTP curves, treasury strips interest rate risk and liquidity risk out of branch operations, centralizing all balance sheet duration risk directly onto the treasury trading desk under executive ALCO oversight.

Simulating a Dual Intraday Stress Shock: The simulator subjects Titan Treasury to a severe dual liquidity and market shock: (1) A sudden $600,000,000 corporate tax clearing outflow strikes at 2:00 PM, depleting the central bank cash account from $2,100,000,000 down to $1,500,000,000—breaching the 90% minimum CRR floor ($1,822,500,000) and creating an immediate $322,500,000 statutory deficit; and (2) Concurrently, central bank policy announcements cause sovereign bond yields to spike by 15 basis points.

Executing the Treasury Crisis Playbook: As Group Treasurer, you execute immediate remedial operations: First, to cure the $322.5M CRR floor breach before the 4:30 PM RTGS window closes, you execute an overnight Tri-Party Repo (TREPS) borrowing of $350,000,000, pledging surplus SLR securities at the overnight repo rate of 6.50% ($62,328 overnight interest cost). The central bank cash account rises to $1,850,000,000, comfortably above the 90% floor and completely eliminating statutory penal interest. Second, the 15 bps yield spike produces a marked-to-market loss of $17,100,000 on the AFS portfolio ($1.14M PV01 * 15 bps) and $1,425,000 on the HFT portfolio ($95K * 15 bps), totaling an $18,525,000 P&L impact. Crucially, the $6.175B HTM book suffers zero write-down, and the $60,000,000 Investment Fluctuation Reserve (IFR) easily absorbs the AFS/HFT loss without impairing regulatory Tier-1 capital.

Regulatory Statutory Returns & Governance Filings: To finalize the operational cycle, treasury operations compiles mandatory statutory filings submitted directly to the central bank. These filings include Form A (reporting fortnightly CRR maintenance under Section 42 of the RBI Act), Form VIII (reporting monthly SLR maintenance under Section 24 of the Banking Regulation Act), and the daily electronic liquidity returns submitted through the e-Kuber core banking portal. The Board of Directors' Risk Management Committee (RMC) receives a comprehensive compliance certification confirming zero reserve defaults, flawless limit discipline, and total capital preservation.

By commanding this integrated treasury simulation, banking executives prove mastery over the operational mechanics, regulatory imperatives, and risk modeling frameworks that preserve institutional solvency in volatile financial markets.
parts.example: Titan Treasury managed a $45B NDTL bank through a dual crisis: an unexpected $600M cash clearing shock was cured by raising $350M in overnight TREPS repo against surplus SLR, while a 15 bps yield spike was absorbed by HTM insulation and the pre-funded Investment Fluctuation Reserve.
parts.code:
def run_titan_enterprise_treasury_simulator(
    ndtl_base: float = 45000000000.0,
    crr_rate: float = 0.045,
    slr_rate: float = 0.18,
    total_securities_held: float = 9500000000.0,
    opening_crr_cash: float = 2100000000.0,
    intraday_clearing_outflow: float = 600000000.0,
    treps_repo_borrowing: float = 350000000.0,
    overnight_repo_rate: float = 0.065,
    afs_pv01: float = 1140000.0,
    hft_pv01: float = 95000.0,
    yield_spike_bps: float = 15.0,
    ifr_reserve_balance: float = 60000000.0
) -> dict:
    # Phase 5 Comprehensive Bank Treasury & Reserve Compliance Engine
    
    # 1. Statutory Requirements
    crr_required_avg = ndtl_base * crr_rate
    crr_min_90_floor = crr_required_avg * 0.90
    slr_required = ndtl_base * slr_rate
    slr_surplus = total_securities_held - slr_required
    
    # 2. Intraday Clearing & Deficit Analysis
    post_shock_cash = opening_crr_cash - intraday_clearing_outflow
    initial_floor_deficit = max(0.0, crr_min_90_floor - post_shock_cash)
    
    # 3. Overnight TREPS Remedy Execution
    final_closing_cash = post_shock_cash + treps_repo_borrowing
    is_crr_floor_satisfied = final_closing_cash >= crr_min_90_floor
    repo_overnight_cost = treps_repo_borrowing * (overnight_repo_rate / 365.0)
    
    # 4. Yield Spike MTM Loss Calculation
    afs_mtm_loss = afs_pv01 * yield_spike_bps
    hft_mtm_loss = hft_pv01 * yield_spike_bps
    total_mtm_hit = afs_mtm_loss + hft_mtm_loss
    
    # IFR Reserve Coverage Check
    remaining_ifr_buffer = ifr_reserve_balance - total_mtm_hit
    is_capital_protected = remaining_ifr_buffer > 0.0
    
    return {
        'audited_ndtl': ndtl_base,
        'crr_daily_average_required': crr_required_avg,
        'crr_min_floor_90pct': crr_min_90_floor,
        'slr_statutory_required': slr_required,
        'slr_surplus_buffer': slr_surplus,
        'post_shock_cash_balance': post_shock_cash,
        'initial_crr_floor_deficit': initial_floor_deficit,
        'treps_repo_liquidity_raised': treps_repo_borrowing,
        'final_closing_crr_cash': final_closing_cash,
        'is_crr_compliant': is_crr_floor_satisfied,
        'repo_overnight_interest_cost': round(repo_overnight_cost, 2),
        'afs_mtm_loss': round(afs_mtm_loss, 2),
        'hft_mtm_loss': round(hft_mtm_loss, 2),
        'total_portfolio_mtm_hit': round(total_mtm_hit, 2),
        'remaining_ifr_cushion': round(remaining_ifr_buffer, 2),
        'treasury_crisis_cleared': is_crr_floor_satisfied and is_capital_protected
    }

titan_treasury = run_titan_enterprise_treasury_simulator()
print("=== Titan National Bank - Enterprise Treasury Command Simulator ===")
print(f"Audited Balance Sheet NDTL:     ${titan_treasury['audited_ndtl']:,.2f}")
print(f"Statutory CRR Daily Average:    ${titan_treasury['crr_daily_average_required']:,.2f}")
print(f"Mandatory 90% CRR Floor:        ${titan_treasury['crr_min_floor_90pct']:,.2f}")
print(f"Statutory SLR Mandate (18%):    ${titan_treasury['slr_statutory_required']:,.2f}")
print(f"Surplus SLR Buffer for Repo:    ${titan_treasury['slr_surplus_buffer']:,.2f}")
print("\n--- Intraday Liquidity Shock & Remedy ---")
print(f"Post-Clearing Outflow Cash:     ${titan_treasury['post_shock_cash_balance']:,.2f}")
print(f"Initial CRR Floor Deficit:      ${titan_treasury['initial_crr_floor_deficit']:,.2f} (Penalty Threat!)")
print(f"TREPS Repo Borrowing Executed:  ${titan_treasury['treps_repo_liquidity_raised']:,.2f} @ 6.50%")
print(f"Final Closing Central Bank Cash:${titan_treasury['final_closing_crr_cash']:,.2f} (Floor: Compliant: {titan_treasury['is_crr_compliant']})")
print(f"Overnight Repo Borrowing Cost:  ${titan_treasury['repo_overnight_interest_cost']:,.2f}")
print("\n--- Market Yield Shock & MTM Valuation ---")
print(f"AFS Portfolio MTM Loss (15 bps):-${titan_treasury['afs_mtm_loss']:,.2f}")
print(f"HFT Portfolio MTM Loss (15 bps):-${titan_treasury['hft_mtm_loss']:,.2f}")
print(f"Total Trading MTM Devaluation:  -${titan_treasury['total_portfolio_mtm_hit']:,.2f}")
print(f"Remaining IFR Capital Cushion:  ${titan_treasury['remaining_ifr_cushion']:,.2f}")
print(f"Enterprise Treasury Status:     {'SOLVENT_COMPLIANT_AND_DE-RISKED' if titan_treasury['treasury_crisis_cleared'] else 'REGULATORY_DISTRESS'}")
